Disease Outbreak Disrupts Madagascar Real Estate Industry Operations

A sudden outbreak of a highly contagious respiratory disease has swept through the real estate industry workforce in Madagascar, causing significant disruption to ongoing site operations and project timelines, industry representatives reported on Thursday.

According to the Madagascar Real Estate Association (MREA), dozens of employees at key property development sites in Antananarivo and Toamasina have fallen ill over the past week, prompting partial or complete shutdowns at several locations. Firms have implemented quarantine protocols and remote work arrangements where possible, but progress on new developments and scheduled property viewings has slowed considerably.

“Approximately 40% of onsite workers at our residential project in Antananarivo are currently absent due to illness or self-isolation,” said Alain Razakarivony, a spokesperson for Majunga Realty. “We have had to halt construction and postpone all client visits until the situation stabilizes. This delay is likely to impact our delivery schedule for at least the next month.”

The outbreak has raised concerns about the safety of both employees and prospective clients at real estate sites. Many agencies, including Tana Properties and Baobab Estates, have temporarily suspended in-person property tours and shifted to virtual showings. “Our foremost priority is the health of our staff and clients,” said Lalao Andrianarisoa, managing director at Tana Properties. “We are following all recommended health guidelines and communicating transparently with our clients about unavoidable delays.”

The MREA estimates that, as of June 19, more than 150 workers across the industry have been affected, with the majority presenting mild to moderate symptoms. However, several cases have required hospitalization, underscoring the seriousness of the outbreak. New site launches have been deferred, and ongoing property management has been reduced to essential maintenance activities.

Industry analysts predict the disruption could have a lasting effect on project pipelines and transaction volumes if the outbreak persists. “The sector’s operational resilience is being tested,” said Feno Rakotomalala, an independent property market analyst. “Firms will need to adapt quickly to minimize further project delays and maintain client confidence.”

The Madagascar Real Estate Association has convened an emergency task force to monitor the situation and coordinate industry-wide responses. The duration and ultimate impact of the outbreak remain uncertain as the situation continues to evolve.
